transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Nova CTO), Maya (Nova Head of Security), Tom (Nova Infra), Rita (Nova Compliance), Chris (Nova SRE), Samir (Redwood CSM)

00:00 Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um for context this is the pen test / patching review that we scoped after the initial security questionnaire. we have priya from engineering and samir on for cs follow up.
00:12 Alex (Nova): yeah thanks, morning — afternoon for some of us. quick ask, we sent the high-level pen test last week, hoping to walk through the findings and map remediation effort to our release windows.
00:25 Priya (Redwood): perfect. we reviewed the vendor PDF — thanks for sharing — and pulled out the triage: a couple of medium risk findings around exposed metadata endpoints, a few S3 misconfig perms but those looked more config on your side, and then a small number of dependency CVEs flagged in the runtime container.
00:45 Maya (Nova): correct, the dependency ones were mostly in one service — the model preprocessor — and we have a patch queued but wanted to confirm the recommended cadence and whether Redwood has runtime mitigations.
01:02 Priya: right, so two paths — short term we can recommend configuration fixes and container image rebuilds, medium term we have mitigations: runtime disable of certain endpoints, stricter RBAC and token expiry tuning. also we have KMS-backed encryption at rest — can confirm key rotation policies if that helps.
01:23 Tom (Nova): can you say more about the RBAC tune? our IAM is fairly coarse today, and we use SAML SSO via Okta.
01:34 Priya: sure. recommended is least-priv role bindings per service, and for Redwood deployments we support SAML/SSO + SCIM provisioning; you can map roles to groups and enforce session timeouts. engineering can push a policy that rejects long-lived service tokens.
01:48 Chris (Nova SRE): ok, that fits. on audit logs — the vendor called out missing retention metadata for certain API calls. how long do you recommend keeping logs for SOC2 & ISO evidence?
02:02 Jordan: typical baseline is 90 days of hot logs and 365 days of retained logs for SOC2 evidence; ISO can require similar retention depending on scope. we can also provide filtered audit exports that show access by token and route.
02:18 Rita (Nova Compliance): good, we'll need proof of immutable audit logs for certain endpoints — can Redwood produce signed audit dumps or is it just CSV exports?
02:28 Priya: we produce time-stamped audit logs with HMAC signatures in the export; for Private deployments you can also integrate with your SIEM via syslog or guaranteed delivery to your S3 bucket with object lock for immutability.
02:45 Alex: about the pen test vendor’s medium finding on the metadata exposure — there's a mention of KV cache keys being accessible in some older runtime builds. is that a Redwood runtime issue or an integration config?
03:00 Priya: from the samples, it looked like an integration misconfig — older clients storing cache blobs in a public bucket. our latest runtime versions harden the KV cache and require signed access. we'll provide specific version notes in the report.
03:17 Maya: ok — if it's a client misconfig then our remediation path is straightforward. the trickier piece is the CVEs in our base image — we have a patch window every two weeks, but some teams push releases monthly. what's Redwood's recommended cadence for critical patches?
03:36 Priya: critical CVEs should be patched within 72 hours ideally; for infra-level dependencies we recommend a biweekly patch cadence and a monthly full rebuild of images. we can help automate image builds via CI hooks — we have example policies for secure SDLC with dependency scanning (SCA) integration.
03:55 Tom: does Redwood run SCA scans on customer images or only on Redwood-managed images?
04:04 Priya: only on Redwood-managed base images; for customer images we can run scans if you provide an artifact or allow a one-off scan during onboarding. many customers integrate their CI scanning and share SCA reports with us.
04:20 Samir (Redwood): can I jump in — one piece that helped other customers was a remediation tracker spreadsheet we send that ties each finding to owner, risk, and target patch window. Jordan will share that after the call.
04:33 Jordan: yep that's in the next steps.
04:36 Alex: nice. on long term — we're interested in Private deployment (VPC) for some flows to meet data residency and HSM needs. the pen test vendor noted a couple of hosting/config issues that would be irrelevant if we moved to Private. what's the typical timeline to get Private up for a pilot?
04:55 Jordan: usually a couple weeks to provision a Private tenant if we have an MSA and infra access; we can also do a Dedicated trial faster for a replay of the pen test if you want to exercise the same workloads.
05:10 Maya: for SOC2 evidence we need audit trail access, KMS key policy review, and encryption-at-rest proofs. can Redwood provide KMS/HSM attestation?
05:22 Priya: we integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / CloudHSM) and can show key access logs. for Redwood-managed keys we provide rotation policy and KMIP-based HSM integration on Private. we'll attach the KMS design doc.
05:38 Rita: and about encryption in transit — the vendor flagged a few services that don't enforce TLS client certs internally. is mutual TLS supported?
05:48 Priya: yes, mutual TLS is supported in Private and Dedicated; hosted API enforces TLS for public endpoints and you can enable mTLS for private peering. we'll include config snippets.
06:05 Alex: great. let's talk remediation priorities — what should we fix first so it doesn't block SOC2 readiness?
06:14 Maya: from our view: 1) close S3 perms and metadata exposure, 2) remediate critical CVEs, 3) enable stricter RBAC and SSO session controls, 4) provide audit export evidence.
06:29 Priya: agreed. for S3 perms we can provide prescriptive policies and a scan to detect publicly accessible objects. for CVEs we recommend image rebuilds and we can assist with a rollback plan.
06:44 Tom: about rollback — do you support canary deploys / A/B to reduce blast radius during patch windows?
06:51 Priya: yes, Redwood runtime supports canary rollouts, model pinning, and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if a deploy fails. that'll help your teams test patches in a small cohort.
07:05 Chris: any suggestions for scheduling patch windows that minimize inference latency impact?
07:12 Priya: schedule batch rebuilds during low traffic, enable autoscale buffers, and use prefix caching to reduce cold start load. we can provide a recommended patch window template based on your token volumes.
07:28 Alex: on vulnerability management process — we currently track in JIRA; vendor opened a PR with remediation suggestions. do you have a preferred workflow for triage mapping to your platform?
07:39 Jordan: typically customers create JIRA tickets with severity mapped to our remediation tracker; we suggest owners and target dates and have a weekly cadence call for P1/P2 items. Samir can help run that.
07:51 Samir: happy to.
07:53 Maya: what about third-party dependencies like the tokenizer lib — vendor flagged CVE-2026-2345 which impacts inference. we're worried about silent model deviations if we bump the tokenizer version.
08:06 Priya: good point — changing tokenizers can change tokenization and results. recommended path is: 1) patch in a canary environment, 2) run eval prompts to check regression, 3) monitor quality metrics before wide release. Redwood Optimize can help with regressions and eval hooks.
08:24 Alex: nice, that helps.
08:27 Tom: on proof of remediation — does Redwood accept penetration re-test evidence or do you run your own verification?
08:34 Priya: we accept vendor re-tests; if you want Redwood to verify post-fix we can run a replay test in a Dedicated trial and validate fixes, but that would be scoped separately.
08:48 Rita: for SOC2 audit scope, auditors will want evidence of developer secure SDLC — do you have docs on code review, SCA, dependency alerts, and patch cadence?
08:59 Priya: yes — we have an SDLC doc that covers PR review gates, static analysis, dependency scanning, and release gating. we'll attach that and an example SCA report.
09:12 Alex: perfect. any blockers for the remediation plan?
09:16 Maya: only that we need the full pen test PDF with appendices to map to our teams. also we want to confirm which findings are false positives.
09:26 Jordan: we'll share the full PDF and an annotated tracker marking false positives and suggested owners.
09:33 Chris: bandwidth question — if we prioritize critical CVEs within 72 hours, do you have recommended resource estimates? like FTE days per critical?
09:44 Priya: it varies — for a simple dependency bump maybe half a day; for compatibility-sensitive libs like tokenizers, maybe 2-5 days including regression eval. we'll put rough estimates in the tracker.
09:58 Alex: timeline-wise, can we target a remediation plan by end of next week?
10:04 Jordan: yes — that'll be the action item; we'll send the tracker by 2026-03-25.
10:09 Priya: also flagged in the pen test was an order-of-operations vulnerability in session termination; that requires a config change and short patch.
10:19 Maya: ok, please prioritize that.
10:21 Tom: last technical q — for KMS we use customer-managed keys in AWS, if we integrate with Redwood, do you maintain any plaintext key material?
10:31 Priya: no, Greenwood — sorry Redwood — never stores plaintext keys; we call KMS APIs and can do envelope encryption. customer-managed keys remain controlled by you. for HSM we can integrate via CloudHSM/KMS.
10:50 Alex: thanks. small aside: vendor mentioned rate-limit misconfig that allowed some token brute forcing on a non-prod endpoint. are rate limits configurable per-route?
11:05 Priya: yes, per-route rate limits, IP allowlists, and WAF rules are all configurable; we recommend restricting non-prod endpoints to internal-only by default.
11:18 Jordan: ok, to recap next steps — I'll send the full report and remediation tracker, Priya will schedule a deep dive for remediation playbook and patch cadence, and Nova will export SCA results and confirm SOC2 evidence scope.
11:34 Maya: agreed.
11:36 Alex: great, thanks everyone.
11:38 Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up in the tracker and set the deep dive.
11:42 Samir: appreciate it, bye.

End of transcript.
